conviction_note: Nothing I found decides this print. The revenue guide is high single digits and the company has beaten revenue consensus in seven straight quarters, but the bar is disputed ($3.38B vs $3.442B), and the stock fell about 13% on two of the last three revenue beats when the margin or the guide disappointed. Third-party data for the category was soft in Q3, and short interest is a moderate ~10% of float. So p_up is 52 on a 13.5% absolute move (the option-implied 12.84% and a 12.75% median reaction, nudged up because a Q4 guide is likely). That gives +0.54, close to the +0.2 sum of the findings, so the two measurements agree that this is a near-non-result.
bar: Disputed revenue bar for Q3 2026. MarketBeat consensus is $3.38B revenue and $0.80 EPS (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/W/earnings/), which implies +8.4% on Q3 2025's $3,117M. Chartmill consensus is $3.442B and $0.77 EPS (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/W/estimates, via search snippet, page 403), which implies +10.4%. The company guide from the 2026-08-04 call is high-single-digit revenue growth (about $3.37-3.40B), gross margin 29.5-30.5% likely at the low end, and adj. EBITDA margin 6-7% (https://quartr.com/events/wayfair-w-q2-2026_3P7axkaf; https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/wayfair-aktie-legt-nach-q2-zu-umsatz-und-eps-uber-erwartungen-q3-wachstum-hoch-einstellige-spanne). The two estimate sources disagree, so every finding is capped small. MarketBeat's $3.38B sits inside the guide; Chartmill's $3.442B sits above its top. Q3 2025 base: revenue $3,117M, adj. EBITDA $208M (6.7%), adj. EPS $0.70 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616707/000161670725000125/a2025-09x30ex991.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest is moderately elevated. Fintel (as of ~2026-10-23) shows 11.95M shares short, 10.44% of float, 6.59 days to cover (https://fintel.io/s/us/W). Massive shows the same 11.95M shares at 2026-09-30 with 4.8 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/w). MarketBeat had 14.90M shares (13.84% of float) at 2026-06-30, so short interest has come down since June. The options market leans nowhere: 25-delta skew +0.22 vol points, put/call OI 1.06, priced_direction_lean 'balanced', event-implied move 12.84%. Tape: spot $111.13, +5.4% over 20 days, -1.6% over 5 days, 7.5% below the 52-week high ($119.98) and 93.6% above the 52-week low. Insiders sold steadily under 10b5-1 plans: 296,024 shares ($30.6M) in the 90 days to 2026-10-08, with Form 144s and Form 4s still being filed up to 2026-11-02.

findings.finding: Wayfair has beaten revenue consensus in each of the last seven quarters, by $0.02B to $0.16B (Q2 2026: $3.52B vs $3.47B). The Q3 guide of high-single-digit growth on a $3,117M base implies about $3.37-3.40B, and the CEO wrote on 2026-08-04 that he expects 'even further acceleration' beyond Q2's 7.5%. Against MarketBeat's $3.38B bar a modest revenue beat is the base case; against Chartmill's $3.442B (+10.4%) it would be an in-line print or a slight miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beat in all seven quarters, yet the stock fell -13.02% on 2026-02-19 and -12.75% on 2026-04-30. Q1 2026 was a revenue beat with an EPS miss and negative FCF (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1617713/wayfairs-nysew-q1-cy2026-beats-on-revenue-but-stock-drops). It rose +29.97% on 2026-08-04 and +23.22% on 2025-10-28 when the beat came with EBITDA and FCF strength. Revenue alone has not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. A seven-quarter beat streak is visible on every terminal, and the 10.4%-growth estimate already embeds a beat over the guide. If the market expected an outsized revenue beat, the skew would lean to calls; it is flat at +0.22.
findings.independence: Company 8-K for Q2 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001616707/000161670726000147/a2026-08x04ex991.htm): US revenue +8.7%, orders +6.0%, active customers +3.3%, Q2 orders up 12% sequentially. This is the company's own document, separate from the estimate aggregator.

findings.finding: Third-party data for the category softened through Q3. The CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor, on a new card-panel methodology, shows furniture and home furnishings sales down 2.7% YoY in September 2026, the only major category to decline. NAR shows August existing-home sales at a two-year low and September at 3.99M SAAR, down YoY in all four regions. Wayfair's growth therefore rests entirely on share gains (it cites a 'high single digit share spread').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wayfair rose +30% in Aug 2026 and +23% in Oct 2025 while the category was weak, because the company said its guide assumed no recovery. Category weakness has not hurt the print when share gains held. The Q1 2026 drop (-12.75%) came with 'choppy demand' commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Both series are public, and Wayfair's Q3 guide already assumed no category recovery. What may not be priced is the Q4 guide: a September category that is negative YoY, with housing at a two-year low, makes it harder to guide holiday growth above Q3. If the market had priced a soft Q4 guide, the 20-day run-up of +5.4% and a stock near its 52-week high would look different.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Housing data from NAR via Mortgage News Daily (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/news/10162026-existing-home-sales-nar-inventory-prices-appr) points the same way. RH guided Q3 revenue +5-6% on 2026-09-10 (https://pulse2.com/rh-q2-revenue-rises-2-6-to-922-2-million-as-company-targets-up-to-7-fiscal-2026-growth/amp/), a slow but positive high-end read.

findings.finding: Q3 gross margin was guided to 29.5-30.5%, 'likely toward the lower end' because of loyalty-program and customer-experience investment. Adj. EBITDA margin was guided to 6-7%, against 6.9% in Q2 2026 and 6.7% in Q3 2025. The guide leaves little room for margin expansion year over year in Q3, and margin is the line the stock has traded on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin and profit drove the large moves: Q1 2026 EPS miss and negative FCF, -12.75%; Q2 2026 EBITDA +18% with record FCF, +29.97%; Q3 2025 EBITDA $208M vs $119M, +23.22%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The comment is inside the company's own guide, and the consensus EPS of $0.77-0.80 vs $0.70 last year already sits inside it. This is filed because the margin line is where this stock's sign has come from, not because the market has missed it.
findings.independence: Goldesel, 2026-08-04 (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/wayfair-aktie-legt-nach-q2-zu-umsatz-und-eps-uber-erwartungen-q3-wachstum-hoch-einstellige-spanne), reports the same guide. Same underlying call, so this is not independent evidence.

findings.finding: Insiders sold steadily into the print under 10b5-1 plans. CEO Niraj Shah sold 69,000 shares at $103.35 on 2026-09-14 (19% of his directly held count), and insiders sold 296,024 shares ($30.6M) in the 90 days to 2026-10-08. EDGAR shows Form 144s on 10-13, 10-15, 10-20 and 10-29 and Form 4s up to 2026-11-02. There were no 8-Ks between the 2026-08-04 earnings filing and today.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Founder/CEO 10b5-1 selling is long-running at Wayfair and was present before both the +30% (Aug 2026) and -13% (Feb 2026) prints. There is no reaction history tied to it.
findings.why_not_priced: These are pre-arranged plans that are publicly filed, so the information content is low. Filed for breadth; it would matter only if the plans were adopted or changed recently, and I did not check that.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions API (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001616707.json) lists the same Form 144/4 cluster from 2026-08-04 to 2026-11-02.

findings.finding: Short interest is about 10.4% of float (11.95M shares) with 4.8-6.6 days to cover, down from 13.8% at 2026-06-30. The last two prints that cleared on margin produced +23% and +30% squeeze-type moves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-28: +23.22% on 5.7x median volume. 2026-08-04: +29.97% on 5.3x median volume. Both upside moves were larger than the downside moves (-13.02%, -12.75%), so the reaction distribution is skewed to the upside.
findings.why_not_priced: The straddle prices the size of the move, not the direction. Skew is flat (+0.22), so the option market is not paying for the upside skew that this name's own history shows, which is a mild case for upside asymmetry if the print is good.
findings.independence: Massive gives the same share count at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/w); MarketBeat gives the June figure (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/W/short-interest/).

findings.finding: Wayfair is retiring its convertibles. It repurchased $145M principal of its 2028 notes in Q2 2026 (a $59M loss on extinguishment, below operating income), cutting the adjusted diluted share count to 147M from 156M. Convertible shares in that count fell to 14M from 27M, and the interest add-back fell to $4M from $13M. Any further Q3 repurchases are a modest tailwind to adjusted EPS per share, with a GAAP loss below the line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 extinguishment loss did not stop a +30% reaction. The market looked through the GAAP charge.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The share-count reduction is in the Q2 release and in the models. Asked what the money buys: it reduces dilution and interest, funded from $1.1B of cash and $301M of quarterly FCF, so it is a small positive and not a distress signal.
findings.independence: Same document as the margin and revenue context; no separate source.

findings.finding: Wayfair's Q4 demand levers are already in motion and the call will report on them. A Way Day sale ran 2026-10-24 to 10-26 with 'up to 80% off', and the Klarna partnership was expanded to 0% APR for up to six months for US customers. Q4 quarter-to-date commentary and a Q4 guide on the call will carry the read on how both landed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Promotional events are recurring, so there is no isolated reaction history. The guide drove the sign on the last four prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither the outcome of the sale nor its margin cost is visible to anyone until the call. The sign is ambiguous: heavy promotion supports Q4 revenue but pressures gross margin, which is already guided to the low end.
findings.independence: Way Day press release, 2026-10-15, as reported in search results (https://www.autobound.ai/companies/wayfair/news). Not company-level data on the outcome.

outside_window.finding: Section 232 tariff increases on upholstered furniture and kitchen cabinets were postponed to 2027-01-01; the rate stays at 25% for now. This affects 2027 cost, not this print, unless the Q4 guide addresses it.
Physical store pipeline: large-format stores in Cincinnati and Princeton in 2027 and Cherry Hill in 2028. Capex timing only.

rejected_candidates.detail: Stale April 2026 estimate, contradicted by current consensus of $0.77-0.80 (Chartmill and MarketBeat) and by Q3 2025's actual $0.70.

baseline_tension: What I found is balanced and agrees with the flat skew. The +5.4% run-up and a stock 7.5% below its high mean expectations are not low, which slightly offsets the upside skew in this name's reaction history, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (disputed bar, $3.38B vs $3.442B) and lesson 1 (revenue beats sold in Feb and Apr 2026): revenue-beat finding cut from +0.6 to +0.4.
Lesson 6 (finding inside the company's own guide): gross-margin-at-low-end finding moved toward 0, from -0.3 to -0.1.
Lesson 5 (proxy is filed small, not dropped): category/housing proxy kept and trimmed from -0.6 to -0.5.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question; what the money buys): convertible-repurchase finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1. It is already in the Q2 share count, and the money reduces dilution rather than signalling distress.
Lesson 7: short interest looked up (10.4% of float); no negative finding is large enough to need shrinking for squeeze risk. Positioning finding left at +0.4.
Net: the pre and post sums are both +0.2; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged.
